title: A Clean Slate for Offline Reinforcement Learning

snippets.content: Progress in offline reinforcement learning (RL) has been impeded by ambiguous problem definitions and entangled algorithmic designs... We develop two algorithms—TD3-AWR (model-free) and MoBRAC (model-based)—which demonstrate improved average performance compared to baselines on selected datasets.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL)—the task of learning effective policies from pre-collected, static datasets... achieving average training speedups of 131.5x and 74.8x against OfflineRL-Kit [16] and CORL [17]... we introduce two novel offline RL methods: TD3-AWR and MoBRAC.
We apply RL to a finite-horizon MDP defined by the tuple <S0, S, A, D, R, T>. D: S x A -> Delta(S) is the transition dynamics... The policy is trained to maximize the expected return J_M^pi.
Offline RL methods use a pre-collected dataset... This dataset consists of transitions (s_i, a_i, r_i, s_{i+1}, a_{i+1}) for i = 1..N... Model-based methods generalize by training a dynamics model.

snippets.location: 3 Refining Evaluation in Offline RL / 3.1 Variants
snippets.content: Taxonomy of offline RL: zero-shot, pre-deployment policy selection (2a), post-deployment policy selection (2b), offline-to-online... we define an offline RL method to include a fixed hyperparameter range which remains constant across datasets.

Rigorous evaluation for Setting 2a under a fixed budget of N pre-deployment interactions... UCB bandit as default tuning algorithm... Recommended Datasets: While MuJoCo locomotion and Adroit tasks from the D4RL suite are popular, limiting evaluation to these risks overfitting hyperparameters to these domains. Instead, we recommend focusing on widely used tasks such as hopper-medium-v2, halfcheetah-medium-expert-v2, walker2d-medium-replay-v2, pen-human-v1, pen-cloned-v1, pen-expert-v1, kitchen-mixed-v0, and maze2d-large-v1 from the canonical D4RL dataset.

Each algorithm is tuned with its original hyperparameter ranges without equalizing the online tuning budgets or computational cost across methods... prior studies often neglect to report or control these tuning budgets, which we continue here for consistency with original papers... Distractor Policy Phenomenon: dips are common artifacts of statistical fluctuations and sampling noise... likely reflect noise rather than fundamental flaws.

Under a transparent evaluation budget, we find that MoBRAC outperforms the other model-based methods in 6 out of 9 datasets and is tied with MOPO for 3 others (Appendix K).
